doc: FBL 0.15, section 4.9 (Terms, read through the body's directives) and 6.3 (A term), spec 067, FR-008: a keyword, a prefix redeclared between two uses, a `\uXXXX` in a term written whole, a relative IRI before and after a base, and a `\` in a local name. A set writes the IRI under the longest declaration whose local name `local` admits, whether in force there or not, a later one winning a tie, else whole, and an undo restores the bytes.

steps.doc: Opening and saving without an edit writes the bytes that were read.
steps.expect:
prefix ex: <http://example.org/> .
ex:a a ex:b .
prefix ex: <http://other.org/> .
ex:a <rel> <http://example.org/one\u0041> .
base <http://base.org/x/> .
<rel> ex:long\.name <../up> .

steps.doc: An IRI whose rest the `local` of the file does not admit is written whole.
steps.expect:
prefix ex: <http://example.org/> .
ex:a a <http://example.org/c/d> .
prefix ex: <http://other.org/> .
ex:a <rel> <http://example.org/one\u0041> .
base <http://base.org/x/> .
<rel> ex:long\.name <../up> .

prefix ex: <http://example.org/> .
ex:a a ex:b .
prefix ex: <http://other.org/> .
ex:a <rel> <http://example.org/one\u0041> .
base <http://base.org/x/> .
<rel> ex:long\.name <../up> .

steps.doc: An IRI under a declared namespace is written under its prefix. `ex:` names two namespaces, and each is found: this one by the first declaration, whose name reads otherwise here, is refused by the read-again check at the second.
steps.expect:

prefix ex: <http://other.org/> .
ex:a <rel> <http://example.org/one\u0041> .

<rel> ex:long\.name ex:up .
